attribution_limitations: The abstract gives the age as 46 years while the case presentation gives 48 years; the source does not reconcile them.
The abstract says the patient was admitted with pleuritic chest pain, whereas the case presentation says he denied any chest pain and that mild shortness of breath started on the day of presentation.
Hemoglobin is printed as 91 g/dL, which is not plausible for the described severe anemia and is probably a print artefact; no second hemoglobin value is printed.

The case text says apixaban was given for long term anticoagulation, while the discussion says the authors decided to anticoagulate for 6 months; "long term" is qualitative, so this is an ambiguity rather than two conflicting numbers, and the source does not relate the two statements.

The clause "that started on the day of presentation" certainly covers the shortness of breath (its nearest noun) but may or may not also cover the dizziness, while the preceding sentence says the listed symptoms developed over two weeks.

The three-month follow-up is anchored to "the diagnosis", which the sentence does not name; the only diagnosis described in that paragraph is the biopsy diagnosis consistent with celiac sprue, and the order of the biopsy diagnosis before the follow-up relies on that reading.
The unit is not printed after the anti-tissue transglutaminase IgG value of 60.1 or after the white cell count and platelet count; only the reference range of the antibody carries a unit.
The abstract says the patient was admitted and the case text says he was referred to the hospital; no admission date, length of stay or discharge is stated.

The hypercoagulability work-up including homocysteine levels revealed no abnormalities, and the discussion says the patient had normal folic acid and homocysteine levels; the source does not say whether the discussion refers to the same homocysteine measurement.
